thread.title_full: Former Petros-Joyner students bused to wrong school and wrong home on first day - NewsBreak

author: Jack Ziskin
title: Former Petros-Joyner students bused to wrong school and wrong home on first day - NewsBreak
text:
By Jack Ziskin ,
5 hours ago
MORGAN COUNTY, Tenn. (WATE) – Petros-Joyner Elementary School closed in May. Parents were given the option to send their child to Wartburg Middle School or Coalfield School, and it all went wrong on the first day of school. Parents said the district wasn’t prepared and hasn’t communicated with them.
On Tuesday, the first day of school, Jamee Tucker put her son on the bus, then she noticed the bus was going the wrong way.
“I text him and said, ‘hey, why are they taking you to Coalfield?’ And he said, ‘no, we’re going down another road to pick up more kids.’ And then once he realized that he wasn’t coming back this way, he sent me another message and said, ‘hey, they’re taking me on to Coalfield and I’m not sure why,'” said Tucker.
A school resource officer later drove her son to the correct school, Wartburg Middle School. She said her son was an hour late.
Tucker is not alone. Amber Foster dropped her nine-year-old daughter, Abrie, off at Wartburg Elementary for her first day at school.
“It was phenomenal until she got on the bus,” said Foster.
Her daughter was supposed to ride home on the same bus as her sisters.
“She got on the bus thinking that she was going to get to drive right home to her house,” said Foster. “And when she got on her two older sisters were not on the bus. And then she started freaking out because they were supposed to ride home with her.”
Foster’s oldest daughter called her, saying her little sister wasn’t with her. Foster leapt into action.
“And so, I had to track my youngest daughter,” said Foster. “Thank god I gave her a phone.”
She said as a mother, it was an upsetting experience.
“You just want to chase the bus down and make it stop to get your kid off because she’s cried,” said Foster. She said school staff were not made aware of proper bus routes, and that the bus driver did not have her youngest daughter on his route. Foster said he not only apologized, but planned to drive her daughter home since he was her bus driver last year.
Director of Schools Jamie Pemberton said the district is working to address the issue.
“We have new routes that we’re running,” said Pemberton. “So, the bus supervisor and myself are working closely together to get some of the kinks that we had on the first day of school.”
He hasn’t spoken to either parent.
“I did not speak to them personally,” said Pemberton.
Both parents have said the school district has failed to communicate with staff and bus drivers, which contributed to the issue.
“I don’t even know that they were aware of it,” said Tucker.
In order to offer all students a bus ride from Petros-Joyner to their new schools, the Coalfield School principal is now driving one of the school buses. Parents are still concerned.
“It’s heartbreaking and it’s frustrating,” said Tucker. “I understand the challenges and stuff like that, but the lack of communication and what we’re supposed to be doing has been non-existent.”
On Wednesday, Tucker dropped her son off at his old school and new bus stop. The bus was ten minutes late. She said the bus garage suggested she have her son change schools after yesterday’s incident. She adds that Petros-Joyner high schoolers used to get picked up at the elementary school.
Pemberton said the decision to close Petros-Joyner saved the district a million dollars, most of which went towards teacher compensation. He said it’s difficult for a rural district to pay teachers $50,000 dollars a year.
Parents said some students had to wait an hour after school for pickup yesterday, and that there have been busing issues in the Sunbright and Deer Lodge area for years, in part due to a shortage of bus drivers.
▶ See more top stories on WATE.com After 6 News visited Morgan County schools’ central office, the district put out an updated bus schedule on Facebook.
6 News reached out to Coalfield’s principal about his new bus route, but the school office said he was driving the bus route so he can memorize it.
